rows.label: Black-box
rows.value: Zero prior knowledge. Simulates an external attacker. Tester starts from only publicly available information — domain name, IP range, nothing more.

rows.label: Grey-box
rows.value: Partial knowledge — e.g. one standard user account or a high-level network diagram. Simulates a compromised insider or a credential-phishing attack.

rows.label: White-box
rows.value: Full knowledge: source code, architecture diagrams, credentials, infrastructure documentation. Most thorough — finds the deepest technical issues fastest.

rows.label: 1. Scoping
rows.value: Define targets, Rules of Engagement, timeline. Written authorisation signed before any testing begins.

rows.label: 2. Reconnaissance
rows.value: OSINT, DNS, WHOIS, LinkedIn, GitHub — passive intelligence only. No packets sent to the target yet.

rows.label: 3. Scanning
rows.value: Nmap (ports/services), Nessus/OpenVAS (CVEs), Nikto (web) — active enumeration within scope.

rows.label: 4. Exploitation
rows.value: Prove real-world impact by exploiting confirmed vulnerabilities. Document every command, timestamp, and output.

rows.label: 5. Reporting
rows.value: CVSS severity scores, proof-of-concept evidence, executive summary, technical findings, remediation roadmap.

rows.label: CVE
rows.value: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures — a public registry entry with a unique ID (e.g. CVE-2017-5638) for each known vulnerability.

rows.label: CVSS
rows.value: Common Vulnerability Scoring System — 0.0 to 10.0. Critical: 9.0–10.0 | High: 7.0–8.9 | Medium: 4.0–6.9 | Low: 0.1–3.9

rows.label: OWASP Top 10
rows.value: The 10 most critical web application security risks. A standard reference for web application penetration testing, updated regularly.

rows.label: PTES
rows.value: Penetration Testing Execution Standard — defines the minimum phases and deliverables expected in a professional engagement.
